game: Week 5 CLE@NYJ / kickoff not saved / spread not saved / total not saved / weather not saved

script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only and no point total is inferred. Over weeks 2-4 CLE is a Judkins run team (47 carries, 144 yards, 3.06 YPC) plus Watson designed runs (19/95, 5.0 YPC), with throws split among Concepcion (23 targets/101 yards), Fannin (20/132) and Boston (19/225). NYJ's run game is a stuck committee — Hall 29/61 (2.10 YPC), Allen 23/80 (3.48 YPC) — so Wilson (25 targets/191 yards) has to carry the offense, with Sadiq and Williams behind him. Base: competitive, neither a shootout nor a clock-kill; both teams run enough to cap ceilings, and the throws that matter are intermediate because both defenses are much worse in the middle than outside.
script.flip1: CLE leads and clocks it with Judkins and Watson. CLE pass-catcher yards stall, NYJ abandons the 2.10-YPC Hall run, and Wilson/Sadiq/Williams targets rise.
script.flip2: NYJ's 37% blitz gets home: Boston's downfield air (269 air yards over L3) dies, quick throws to Fannin, Concepcion and Judkins (–29 air, checkdown profile) go up, and it becomes a short-area grind. Other flip is a middle-of-field shootout — both QBs live in the soft middle (NYJ 9.26 YPA, CLE 9.47) and the intermediate options clear together.

Watson's 19 carries mean he is the active QB in this window. No snap or rep limits are listed.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits are the proxy: NYJ allows 9.26 YPA in the middle (35 att) vs 5.83 left (42) and 5.06 right (50). CLE allows 9.47 middle (30 att) vs 6.19 left (59) and 6.69 right (55). Both are sounder outside than inside, so the matchup is hook/middle/slot, not the outside corner.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitz rate 37%; CLE blitz rate 24%. CLE QB EPA/dropback is 0.14 vs blitz (n=51) and 0.15 with no blitz, so the blitz does not collapse Cleveland — it should shorten throws. NYJ QB is 0.12 vs blitz (n=35) and 0.14 without. No pressure rate, sack count or time-to-throw beyond those splits. Expectation: deep yards down, TE/RB and intermediate catches up, especially for CLE into the higher blitz rate.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ rush defense: 4.50 YPC, 12 runs of 10+ in four games, only 9 passes of 20+ on 136 attempts (6.6%). CLE rush defense: 4.67 YPC, 15 runs of 10+, 15 passes of 20+ on 157 attempts (9.6%). CLE is leakier on explosives and on the ground. Both bleed the middle; NYJ is the tougher downfield defense and the softer outside-YPA defense.
matchup.overlap: Boston (269 air yards, 75 rec yds/game) attacks the thing NYJ does best — suppressing 20+ plays and holding outside YPA to 5.06/5.83 — so that is a bad overlap, not an edge. The good CLE overlap is Fannin (20 targets, 130 air yards, 44 rec yds/game), an intermediate weapon into NYJ's 9.26 middle and 37% blitz. On NYJ's side Wilson is the primary (238 air yards) into CLE's explosive leak, but 68.5 already sits above his 63.7 L3 average. Williams (128 rec yards on 77 air, YAC-heavy, 11 targets) is the secondary option whose line has not caught the recent role, into the same soft middle.

NYJ: Hall 29/61 (2.10 YPC, ~20 rush yds/game) is a script problem if they keep feeding him; Allen 23/80 (~26.7) and 6 targets/19 rec yards, nowhere near a 71.5 or 89.5 role on this form. Mitchell 12/63/178 is air without the production.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Fannin is already a real intermediate weapon at 44 receiving yards a game, and he is the Brown who attacks the exact zone the Jets bleed — the middle at 9.26 YPA — while a 37% blitz shortens throws toward him rather than breaking a QB who has been fine vs the blitz (0.14 EPA).
edge_players.must_be_true: Fannin keeps the recent route share (about 6-7 targets, not a blocking-only day), Watson stays the QB, and CLE does not turn this into a pure Judkins/Watson clock-kill. Script-dependent: the over needs CLE to keep throwing.
edge_players.kills_it: CLE leads early and runs it (Judkins already at ~16 carries a game), or the Jets rob the middle and Fannin's 130 air yards get treated like Boston's deep shots — NYJ has allowed only 9 passes of 20+ on 136 attempts. A missing price also means this cannot be sized.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Williams has averaged 42.7 receiving yards over the last three games, more than 20 yards above a 22.5 line, and Cleveland is the leakier pass defense here (9.47 YPA in the middle, 15 explosives on 157 throws), so he only needs a reduced version of that role.
edge_players.must_be_true: The 128 yards are not one long play — there is no game log to prove that — and he still gets about 3 targets. NYJ's broken run (Hall 2.10 YPC) keeps them throwing even if the script flips negative.
edge_players.kills_it: A one-play spike plus a 1-2 target day, or Wilson and Sadiq soaking the soft middle so Williams is the buried fourth option (he is only 4th in NYJ targets at 11). A true defensive slog, which the pack cannot confirm because the total is missing, also kills a thin-volume yards leg.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot size a rung and no model probability is being trusted (nothing in the 70%+ band to discount). Directional form agrees with both leans: Fannin 132/3 = 44.0 vs 35; Williams 128/3 = 42.7 vs 22.5. Matchup agrees on the middle (NYJ 9.26, CLE 9.47) and on NYJ's 37% blitz helping intermediate throws. Partial caution, not a cut: NYJ's 9/136 rate of 20+ plays can trim Fannin's 6.5 air yards/target, which is why he stays a lean rather than a strong read. Dropped leans where data disagreed: Judkins under 59.5 (his 48-yard average vs a defense allowing 4.50 YPC), Boston over 47.5 (75-yard average vs that same 6.6% explosive rate — number is soft but the skill he uses is what NYJ takes away), Wilson over 68.5 (63.7 average already under the line). Allen under 71.5 was not taken: L3 says 26.7 rush yards, but a two-way -113 line at 71.5 means the market has role news this pack does not, and an average-only under is the failure mode this process rejects.

Do not substitute Boston recyds 47.5 (-113/-113.5), Judkins rush 59.5 (-114/-112.5), or Allen rush 71.5 (-113/-113) — those numbers were considered and passed.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Williams' 128 yards were one chunk catch buried in the three-game total; he saw two targets, Wilson and Sadiq took the middle CLE actually bleeds, and a 22.5 line that looked soft was a trap on 3.7 targets a game. Fannin blocked: CLE did what the carry log already showed, handing Judkins another 16 rushes and Watson another handful of clock runs, and the Jets' low explosive rate (9 of 136) turned his 130 air yards into a 3-catch, low-20s day instead of a middle-zone feast. We also had no charting to prove either player actually aligns in the middle, no price on Fannin, and no total to tell us the book already expected a slog. The counter-case is real enough that both stay leans, not building blocks for a bigger slip.
slip_story: One story only: both secondaries bleed the middle, so intermediate yards clear soft rungs — Fannin into NYJ's 9.26 middle and 37% blitz, Williams into CLE's 9.47 middle and higher explosive rate, with NYJ's 2.10-YPC Hall run forcing throws if they fall behind. That is the competitive or CLE-ahead script, not a clock-kill slog and not a Boston deep-shot stack (that needs the explosives NYJ suppresses). Do not pair these with a total under, with Allen's rush overs, or with Judkins under. Fannin is the script-dependent leg; Williams is the one that survives the NYJ-trails flip. Two leans, no TD, one market per player. Missing weather means this is not a wind/rain under stack.
